cards.title: One theme contract: every theme x skin binding set proven complete and legible
acceptance: theme-contract: the binding sets are derived, not listed: THEMES (stores/shell.ts) x SKINS read against styles/skins/*.css -> exactly [athena/dark, athena/light, loop-tide/dark, loop-tide/light]; a SKINS entry with no sheet, or a sheet with no SKINS entry, fails naming it

theme-contract over the real app.css + loop-tide.css: every text pair (--foreground and --muted-foreground on --background/--card-bg/--card-raised/--recessed; --accent-text and --primary on --background/--card-bg/--recessed; --primary-fg on --primary; --on-primary on --btn-primary) is >= 4.5:1 and every graphic pair (--status-success/-warning/-error/-info/-pending/-neutral and --focus on --card-bg/--recessed) is >= 3:1 in all four sets -> 0 failures (measured today: 0 of 4 sets fail)

negative control, one-state binding: a fixture skin sheet whose `:root[data-skin=x]` block sets --status-info and whose light block omits it -> the contract reports `x/light: --status-info takes the skin's dark value` (the light block inherits the skin's dark block at (0,2,0), above the base light block at (0,1,0))

zero input is fatal: the contract handed a sheet with no theme block -> throws `no binding set`, never returns an empty, green result

cards.body:
## Summary
The colour contract is held in three different shapes: the base themes check one pair, the Loop Tide skin hand-lists fourteen and copies the maths, and the per-state completeness that a layered skin depends on is checked nowhere. Put the contract in one module, derive the binding sets from THEMES x SKINS, and run every set through it.

## Description
`styles/theme-contract.ts` parses app.css and every sheet in `styles/skins/` (one brace-depth parser, the one loop-tide.css.test.ts already wrote), resolves each binding set through the real cascade (base dark -> base light -> skin dark -> skin light, var() chains followed), and checks one declared pair list: text at 4.5:1, graphics at 3:1 (design-tokens golden path, 'the contrast floor is in the contract': a gate that reads the actual theme definitions and runs on every theme). It also reports a role a skin binds in one state only, which is the defect theme-architecture names ('binding defined in only one state') and which the skin's selector specificity makes silent. The two existing tests drop their copies of the maths. `styles/skins/index.ts` eagerly globs the skin sheets, so the three entries stop naming them and a second skin really is one sheet plus one SKINS entry. The dead app.css exemption in source-guards goes, closing the recorded quality-gates deviation.

## Flow
- theme-contract.ts: parse -> binding sets from THEMES x SKINS -> resolve -> pairs -> findings
- theme-contract.test.ts: real sheets pass; three fixture sheets go red (one-state, floor, unresolved); empty input throws
- motion-tokens.test.ts and loop-tide.css.test.ts keep their non-contrast rules only
- skins/index.ts + three entry imports

## Expected impact
Every claimed ratio in both sheets becomes a checked one; a third skin, or a light-theme edit to Loop Tide, cannot ship an unreadable pair or a dark-only role without a red test. The contract is the place the next appearance axis (BACKLOG's high-contrast theme) attaches.

## Evaluation
Claim: the contract covers 4 binding sets x 26 pairs from one list and catches the two defect shapes no current test can see
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (module absent); today 3 base checks + 14 skin checks, 0 per-state completeness checks
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases, with cases 3-6 as seeded-red negative controls
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence: Scratch measurement over the real sheets (cascade resolved, var() followed): athena dark ok, athena light ok, loop-tide dark ok, loop-tide light ok across the 26 pairs above; skin dark-only roles [] / light-only []; base dark-only [--line, --line-strong, --wash] (var() aliases). grep: `color: var(--accent)` in app.css -> 0 hits, so source-guards.test.ts:26's exemption guards nothing. grep `function ratio|luminance` in tests -> motion-tokens.test.ts and skins/loop-tide.css.test.ts. grep `skins/loop-tide.css` in non-test src -> athena.tsx:34, chrome.tsx:12, preview.tsx:39.

cards.title: The first frame wears the person's theme, skin, text size and motion
shared_surfaces: docs/adr/NNNN-the-first-frame-wears-the-persons-appearance.md (a second, cached copy of four settings rows in webview storage is a decision a reader could question; the store stays the authority)
acceptance: bootAppearance(snapshot {theme:'light', skin:'loop-tide', typeScale:'large', motion:'calm'}, prefersLight=false, prefersReduced=false) -> <html> carries data-theme=light, data-skin=loop-tide, data-type-scale=large, data-motion=calm

three-state theme: snapshot theme 'system' -> data-theme=light when (prefers-color-scheme: light) matches and dark when it does not; for every ThemeChoice x prefersLight the boot's answer equals stores/settings resolveTheme (gated mirror, not a trusted copy)
motion parity: for every MotionChoice x prefersReduced the boot's data-motion equals lib/motion resolveMotion; for every skin/type-scale value the boot accepts exactly what isSkin/isTypeScale accept
no snapshot, corrupt JSON, an unknown skin, or a storage accessor that throws -> boot stamps nothing beyond the HTML's own data-theme=dark and does not throw (today's first frame, unchanged)

followAppearance: useSettings goes hydrated with theme 'light', skin 'loop-tide', typeScale 'large', motion 'calm' -> storage holds exactly that snapshot (the choice 'system' is stored as 'system', never as its resolution)
followAppearance before hydration, or after a refused first read (hydrated false, problem set) -> the stored snapshot is untouched, so a default can never overwrite the person's appearance
the store stays authority: boot stamps light from a stale snapshot, then a hydrate reading theme 'dark' -> data-theme=dark and the snapshot now says dark

vite plugin transformIndexHtml: chrome.html and athena.html come back with the boot as an inline classic script first in <head>, before any stylesheet or module script; preview.html and halo.html come back unchanged (the harness reads its own ?theme=&skin=)
premise: apps/desktop/chrome.html:7 and apps/desktop/athena.html:5 - both documents hard-code data-theme="dark" and set no data-skin, data-type-scale or data-motion

apps/desktop/src/console/root.tsx:29 - the console's first effect calls startShell(), which paints the store defaults (apps/desktop/src/stores/shell.ts:54-55: theme 'dark', skin 'athena') before anything is read

apps/desktop/src/stores/settings.ts:256-287 - the person's theme, text size, motion and skin are applied only after ten awaited store reads over IPC (readRows), i.e. after React has committed the stage in the default appearance
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:336 - Main is created visible on every launch after the first, so that default frame is on screen

apps/desktop/src/styles/app.css:149-163 - data-type-scale moves every size under the headings, so a 'large' or 'compact' person sees the chrome reflow when the row lands; apps/desktop/src/styles/skins/loop-tide.css:146 starts a 1.6 s fade that an in-app Calm choice only stops once data-motion arrives
apps/desktop/src/lib/execute.ts:130 - a localStorage mirror of store-held state already exists as precedent in this webview
cards.rollback: Revert the series: the boot and follow modules, their tests and the ADR are new; the vite plugin and the two entry calls go with the revert. A leftover storage key is inert (nothing reads it), so no cleanup is required.

cards.body:
## Summary
Every launch paints Main in dark teal at the default text size and full motion, then snaps to what the person chose once ten IPC reads come back. A light-theme person gets a dark flash, a Loop Tide person a teal one, a large-text person a reflow, and a person who chose Calm a fade they asked not to see. The app already knows the answer from the last session; stamp it before the first paint.

## Description
`appearance-boot.ts` exports a self-contained `bootAppearance` (no imports, so it can be inlined) that reads one storage key holding the last hydrated choices {theme, skin, typeScale, motion}, resolves `system` against the media queries (theme-architecture: the follow-the-platform state is part of the model and must be stamped before first paint), and sets the four root attributes. A vite plugin in `vite.config.ts` inlines it as the first script in the head of chrome.html and athena.html. `appearance-follow.ts` subscribes to `useSettings` and writes the snapshot only from hydrated state; chrome.tsx and athena.tsx start it. The settings table stays the authority: readRows still applies what it reads, and the snapshot follows. Because the boot is a hand-written mirror of resolveTheme/resolveMotion/isSkin/isTypeScale, parity tests hold it to them (design-tokens cross-language-token-parity: a mirror is gated, never trusted).

## Flow
- launch -> head script reads snapshot -> four attributes set -> stylesheet paints the right appearance
- React mounts -> startShell/readRows -> store rows applied (normally identical: no visible change)
- person changes Theme/Text size/Motion/Style in Look, or the other window does -> hydrated state changes -> snapshot rewritten

## Expected impact
The person's appearance holds from the first frame in both windows at every launch; no dark flash for light users, no chrome reflow for large or compact text, Calm honoured before the first animation starts.

## Evaluation
Claim: the first frame carries the person's last choices, and the store remains the authority
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no boot, no snapshot; the first frame is always dark/athena/comfortable/full)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases (jsdom with a stubbed matchMedia and storage; the plugin called on the HTML text)
Result: better
Gate: none
